API reference¶

Data loading¶

Load the NASA/UCI Airfoil Self-Noise dataset.

The dataset contains 1503 aerodynamic/acoustic measurements of NACA 0012 airfoils taken in a wind tunnel. Five input features describe the test conditions and one target, the scaled sound pressure level, describes the measured noise.

The Excel file is expected at data/airfoil_self_noise.xlsx. It is not committed to the repository and must be kept locally, as noted in the project README.

Example

>>> from functions.data_loader import load_airfoil_data
>>> df = load_airfoil_data()
>>> df.columns.tolist()[-1]
'spl_db'
functions.data_loader.DATA_PATH = WindowsPath('C:/Users/vasbr/OneDrive/Desktop/uni mech eng/2026s2/mma3001 numerical methods and machine learning/mma3001project/nummethodproject/data/airfoil_self_noise.xlsx')¶

<project root>/data/airfoil_self_noise.xlsx.

Type:

Default location of the dataset

functions.data_loader.COLUMN_RENAME = {'attack-angle (deg)': 'attack_angle_deg', 'chord-length (m)': 'chord_length_m', 'free-stream-velocity (m/s)': 'velocity_mps', 'frequency (Hz)': 'frequency_hz', 'scaled-sound-pressure (dB)': 'spl_db', 'suction-side-displacement-thickness (m)': 'disp_thickness_m'}¶

Mapping from the verbose source column headers to short, code-friendly names. Unit suffixes (_hz, _deg, _m, _mps, _db) are kept in the new names so units are never ambiguous downstream.

functions.data_loader.TARGET = 'spl_db'¶

Name of the target column (scaled sound pressure level, dB).

functions.data_loader.FEATURES = ['frequency_hz', 'attack_angle_deg', 'chord_length_m', 'velocity_mps', 'disp_thickness_m']¶

Input feature columns, in the order they appear in the dataset.

functions.data_loader.load_airfoil_data(path: Path = WindowsPath('C:/Users/vasbr/OneDrive/Desktop/uni mech eng/2026s2/mma3001 numerical methods and machine learning/mma3001project/nummethodproject/data/airfoil_self_noise.xlsx')) → pandas.DataFrame[source]¶

Load and clean the airfoil self-noise dataset.

Reads the Excel file, drops the Source.Name column that Power Query style exports add (if present), and renames the remaining columns according to COLUMN_RENAME.

Parameters:

path – Location of the .xlsx file. Defaults to DATA_PATH.

Returns:

A DataFrame with one row per measurement and the columns frequency_hz, attack_angle_deg, chord_length_m, velocity_mps, disp_thickness_m (features) and spl_db (target).

Raises:

FileNotFoundError – If no file exists at path.

Physics features¶

Physics-derived features for the airfoil self-noise dataset.

The raw inputs are dimensional, but airfoil noise is governed largely by dimensionless groups. This module adds three engineered features computed row-wise from the raw columns, so they are recomputed on every load rather than stored in the Excel file.

Example

>>> from functions.data_loader import load_airfoil_data
>>> from functions.physics_features import add_physics_features
>>> df = add_physics_features(load_airfoil_data())
>>> df[["log_frequency", "strouhal", "reynolds"]].shape[1]
3
functions.physics_features.KINEMATIC_VISCOSITY_M2PS = 1.5e-05¶

Kinematic viscosity of air at roughly 20 °C (m^2/s), used for the Reynolds number. The wind-tunnel temperature is not recorded in the dataset, so a standard room-temperature value is assumed.

functions.physics_features.PHYSICS_FEATURES = ['log_frequency', 'strouhal', 'reynolds']¶

Names of the columns added by add_physics_features().

functions.physics_features.add_physics_features(df: pandas.DataFrame) → pandas.DataFrame[source]¶

Return a copy of the dataset with physics-derived feature columns.

Adds:

  • log_frequency: log10(frequency_hz). Frequencies span about two decades, and acoustic spectra are naturally read on a log axis.

  • strouhal: frequency_hz * disp_thickness_m / velocity_mps. Uses the suction-side displacement thickness as the length scale, the scaling used for turbulent boundary-layer trailing-edge noise in the Brooks-Pope-Marcolini (BPM) model.

  • reynolds: velocity_mps * chord_length_m / nu, the chord-based Reynolds number with nu = KINEMATIC_VISCOSITY_M2PS.

Each feature depends only on its own row, so adding them before the train/validation/test split does not leak information between sets.

Parameters:

df – Dataset as returned by functions.data_loader.load_airfoil_data().

Returns:

A new DataFrame with the original columns plus the columns listed in PHYSICS_FEATURES. The input DataFrame is not modified.

Exploratory plots¶

Overview scatter plot of SPL against every input feature.

functions.plot_spl_vs_features.plot_spl_vs_features(df: pandas.DataFrame) → matplotlib.figure.Figure[source]¶

Plot SPL against every input feature on a 2x3 grid.

Frequency spans several decades, so its axis is log-scaled. The unused sixth panel is hidden.

Parameters:

df – Dataset as returned by functions.data_loader.load_airfoil_data().

Returns:

The created matplotlib figure (not yet shown).

Scatter plots of SPL against each feature, split by chord length.

functions.plot_spl_by_chord_length.plot_spl_by_chord_length(df: pandas.DataFrame) → matplotlib.figure.Figure[source]¶

Plot SPL against each non-chord feature, one row per chord length.

Chord length takes only a handful of discrete values, so splitting by it reveals trends that are blurred in the pooled overview plot. The y-axis is shared so noise levels are comparable across rows.

Parameters:

df – Dataset as returned by functions.data_loader.load_airfoil_data().

Returns:

The created matplotlib figure (not yet shown).

Entry point that displays the exploratory plots for the airfoil dataset.

The plotting functions live in their own modules (functions.plot_spl_vs_features and functions.plot_spl_by_chord_length); this script just loads the data and shows both figures:

python src/explore_plots.py
explore_plots.main() → None[source]¶

Load the dataset and display both exploratory figures.
